decisions.justification: The user was asked whether an externally occupied target should abort, be skipped, or be replaced, and selected “Abort upfront.”
The runtime-failure question explicitly asked whether to roll back the run or leave completed renames, and the user selected rollback.
The repeat-run question asked how source-to-same-name steps should behave, and the user selected successful no-ops.
The final contract-confirmation question explicitly included “safe moves through planned-name chains,” which the user approved.
The user was asked what a repeated command producing self-renames should do and selected “No-op success.”
No question, repository resolution, or volunteered answer addressed case-only renames on case-insensitive filesystems.
The stdout-policy question asked whether rejected plans should print proposed mappings, and the user selected output only after success.
The session never asked whether preview or confirmation should be part of the fix or whether safety could depend on operator review.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr

notes: The session clearly declared a bounded path, avoided forbidden questions, and implemented most explicitly settled behavior with focused tests. It missed case-insensitive filesystem semantics and preview policy, while the implementation cannot strictly guarantee either acceptance requirement because preflight-to-rename races can overwrite a newly created target and rollback is explicitly allowed to fail incompletely.
